title: Capacity Allocation

story.briefing: One transport, a fixed mass allowance, and a yard full of salvage. Each piece can be taken once or left. Maximise the value carried.
story.success: Transport loaded to maximum value. The yard signs it off.

description: Given arrays of item masses and item values of equal length, and a mass capacity, choose a subset of items whose total mass does not exceed the capacity while maximising total value. Each item may be taken at most once. Return the largest achievable value.

examples.explanation: Only one item fits; the heavier one is worth more.

hints: Taking items in order of value, or of value per unit mass, both fail — each item is all or nothing, so a greedy choice can block a better pair.
For every item there are two branches: take it, using up its mass, or leave it. Track the best value achievable for each remaining capacity.
Keep an array indexed by capacity. For each item, update that array once. Sweep the capacities downward while doing so, or the same item will be taken more than once.
